✦WINTERGATE
CalendarPlay a roomGame blueprint

Production-ready direction

Build one excellent door first.

The concept is strong, but 24 multi-hour 3D chapters is closer to a full studio production than a small seasonal game. Prototype one 60–90 minute “vertical slice,” prove the puzzle language, then scale.

Recommended stack

Unity + C#

Best first choice for a simultaneous Windows and macOS release with a later Quest port. Use URP, the Input System, Timeline, Addressables, localization tables and OpenXR. Keep interaction physics deterministic and performance budgets Quest-friendly from day one.

Unity 6 LTSC#URPOpenXRSteamworks

Alternative

Godot + GDScript/C#

Excellent for lower cost and open-source control. A good PC/Mac choice, but validate the exact Quest export and store workflow before committing. Unreal is visually powerful but heavier than this stylised puzzle game needs.

Core architecture

CalendarService owns availability; ProgressService stores completion; each chapter is addressable content; puzzle components communicate through simple signals.

Save & unlock

Local JSON save plus Steam Cloud. A chapter opens only when its release date has passed and the previous chapter is complete. Replay never re-locks content.

Cheat & accessibility

Ship supported caretaker codes: YULE-KEY unlocks the next day; RAVEN-24 unlocks everything. Mark the save as assisted, but never disable achievements globally.

Artwork

A theatrical storybook, not realism

Carved silhouettes, bold colour blocking and stage-like rooms keep assets reusable while letting each mythology feel distinct.

Norse mythology

Blue-black stone, iron mechanisms, aurora light, carved runes. Comedy comes from cosmic institutions behaving like understaffed utilities.

1001 Nights

Indigo night, brass astronomy, tiled geometry and animated shadows. Treat the source tradition broadly and respectfully; use a cultural consultant.

Famous fairy tales

Paper-cut forests, theatrical flats, impossible domestic scale. Use public-domain story foundations and original visual designs.

Animal kingdom

Natural materials and clever non-human spaces. Animals speak, but their puzzles arise from real traits: migration, echolocation, camouflage and collective motion.

Reusable art kit

Build modular floors, arches, doors, tracks, sockets, mirrors, weighted plates and light receivers. Theme them through materials, props, lighting, sound and character animation rather than rebuilding mechanics four times.

Puzzle language

Learn in seconds, combine for hours

SystemRuleExample chapterEscalation
Light & mirrorsRedirect beams; colour changes when beams combine.The Brass MoonMoving shadows block paths while a djinn “helpfully” rotates one mirror.
Weight & balanceEverything has a visible weight class.Three Bears, One ThermostatHeat changes object weight, so “just right” becomes a physical rule.
Sound & echoSounds travel, bounce and wake mechanisms.The Parliament of OwlsBuild a call-and-response path while avoiding sleeping delegates.
Cause & sequenceActions repeat on a short loop.Loki's Very Honest MazeCoordinate with your previous loop while Loki changes labels, not rules.
Flow & pressurePipes visibly carry wind, water or sand.Beaver Dam BureaucracyOne resource solves several rooms; routing it creates meaningful tradeoffs.

Design rule: introduce at most one new verb per chapter. Difficulty should come from combining known rules, observing consequences and forming a plan—not from hidden objects, pixel hunting or obscure trivia.

Story & tone

Original jokes inside old stories

Humour target

Write for ages 12 and up: quick banter, genre awareness, bureaucracy jokes, game conventions and gentle anachronisms. Avoid direct references to protected characters, brands, movie dialogue or contemporary memes that will date quickly.

“The prophecy said a hero would come.”
“It also said Tuesday. Prophecies are more guidelines than service guarantees.”

Season arc

Days 1–6 reveal broken rules; 7–12 expose a saboteur; 13–18 show that the Star-Keeper broke the calendar deliberately; 19–23 ask whether the system should be restored; day 24 lets the player rebuild a kinder calendar from every mastered mechanic.

Scope & release

The practical version

Vertical slice

One polished Norse chapter, 60–90 minutes, plus calendar shell and save system.

Season one

Release 8 substantial chapters across December, with small story gifts on intervening days.

Full calendar

Expand to 24 only after measured completion rates, playtime and production cost.

Quest edition

Redesign interaction and locomotion for VR; do not treat it as a one-click port.

Platform plan

Launch Windows and macOS together on Steam. Build with keyboard/mouse and controller parity. For Quest, target OpenXR, baked lighting, simplified shaders, low draw calls and comfortable snap-turn/teleport options.

Calendar rules

Use the player’s trusted local date with a monotonic “latest unlocked date” so clock changes cannot re-lock content. After 24 December—or in off-season mode—offer “Open Calendar” so buyers can play without waiting a year.
